teach_overlay.label: PCR EXPONENTIAL DOUBLING: 1 DNA STRAND → 1,024 (10 CYCLES) → 1,073,741,824 COPIES (30 CYCLES = 2^30)
teach_overlay.detail: Inked PCR exponential amplification & thermal-cycle graph on period paper showing 3-step cycling (95 °C unzip, 54 °C anneal, 72 °C Taq copy) multiplying 1 target DNA molecule by 2^30 = 1,073,741,824 copies in 30 cycles while Taq polymerase retains activity at 75–80 °C
teach_overlay.scale: searching for one gene inside all three billion letters of human DNA without PCR is like hunting for a single needle in a haystack the size of a stadium — whereas thirty cycles of PCR turn that needle into a billion-needle mountain while leaving the hay behind

teach_overlay.scale: ninety-five degrees Celsius is five degrees below boiling water — hot enough to cook an egg white solid in seconds, yet Yellowstone's Taq enzyme copies DNA right through the heat without flinching
